newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: A massive 7.4 billion rand jump in South African May gold and foreign reserves data underlined a strong stock market on Tuesday, although shares tipped off their peaks towards the close on profit-taking.
Futures-related appetite for shares also aided blue-chips' gains with heavyweight financial stocks a favourite, propelling the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's financial index to a new closing high.

Dealers and analysts said local institutions, who have held to the sidelines in recent weeks amid a slew of poor company results, returned as strong buyers further encouraged by renewed talk of an interest rate cut as soon as the third quarter.
"Things are looking up," said Willi Jonker, executive director of portfolio management, Norwich Investments.
"Although concerns remain over lower earnings from corporates in an environment of slower economic growth, that concern is outweighed by a better interest rate outlook," he said.
Second line stocks were also snapped up, dealers said.
"There was a lot of interest in the traditional blue-chips, but the smaller cap stocks, like Aflife and Super Group, also moved up strongly."
Aflife put on 200 cents to a hew high of 29.10 rand and Super Group rose 24 cents to 828 cents.

RMB Holdings surged 3.5 percent to 11.60, off its intraday best of 11.80, on news it was to enter the retail market. This coupled with a five rand rise in Standard to 210 rand lifted the financial index nearly 100 points.
The industrial index finished up 46.4 points at 8,336.8.
Robust gains in heavyweights Anglo, which announced a 23 percent rise in year headline earnings per share, and De Beers, helped the all-share index up 50.7 to 7,112.0.
Figures released late on Monday show South Africa's official reserves soared 51 percent to a record high of 21.8 billion rand in May, streets ahead of the consensus forecast of 17.7 billion.

The increase, boosted by inflows from the privatisation of telecommunications concern Telkom, lifted the country's import cover to more than two months for the first time since the rand crisis broke early last year.
On the stock market's gold board, activity was overshadowed by industrials' performance. The gold index dipped 8.4 to 1,158.2 as bullion slipped below the $344 level.
Overall market turnover on Tuesday was average at around 672 million rand following a dull session on Monday.

Other features included Usko, for the second day in a row seeing heavy volumes of over five million shares on speculation of a take-over. Bonnita slid a further 6.6 percent to 224 cents after poor results on Friday.
Stocks were seen firm for the third consecutive day on Wednesday, supported by continued institutional interest.
Equity futures, drawing strength from the reserves figure and the resulting gains on the rand and bond markets, were firm throughout the day, although gold contracts were lacklustre.
Dealers said activity would become more volatile ahead of the close-out of the June contracts in two weeks time.
The near-month industrial contract was last at 8,041/44 from 7,971, the all-share contract was at 6,455/65 from 6,373 and the gold contract was at 810/20 from 814.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
